assumptions.description: Additive penalties for access and support barriers.
assumptions.name: adherence.access_effect
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. Signs are well supported; magnitudes are not fitted.

assumptions.description: Clamp on derived adherence. Nobody is modelled as perfectly zero.
assumptions.name: adherence.bounds
assumptions.source: Modelling convention.

assumptions.description: Additive shift to baseline adherence by health-literacy band.
assumptions.name: adherence.literacy_effect
assumptions.source: Expert judgement, directionally consistent with adherence literature.

assumptions.description: Penalty per medication beyond `free_medications`, plus draw noise.
assumptions.name: adherence.pill_burden
assumptions.source: Expert judgement; polypharmacy-adherence relationship is real, slope is not.

assumptions.description: Weight contributed by each barrier when present. Summed, then scaled by protocol intensity, then clamped to [0, 1].
assumptions.name: burden.factor_weights
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. Ordering is defensible; absolute weights are not.

assumptions.description: Multiplier applied to the summed barrier weight as the protocol gets heavier. Amplifies existing barriers; adds nothing to a persona with none.
assumptions.name: burden.protocol_intensity
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. The multiplicative form is a modelling choice.

assumptions.description: Cut-points at which a barrier counts as present.
assumptions.name: burden.trigger_thresholds
assumptions.source: Expert judgement; conventional round numbers, not derived cut-points.

assumptions.description: Comorbidity prevalence is scaled by intercept + slope*(age - pivot). Independent Bernoulli draws — correlation structure is NOT modelled.
assumptions.name: cohort.comorbidity_age_factor
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. The independence assumption is a known limitation.

assumptions.description: Per-condition age/sex/stage/comorbidity/biomarker priors in cohort/epidemiology.py. Order-of-magnitude literature ballparks.
assumptions.name: cohort.condition_priors
assumptions.source: Compiled from published prevalence summaries; not fitted to any dataset.

assumptions.description: Validity gate on the trait correlation matrix. Loading fails if the minimum eigenvalue falls below `min_eigenvalue`. Projection to the nearest PSD matrix is DISABLED by default and is never silent: enabling it returns the exact list of pairs that moved and by how much, which must then be recorded here as a correction. A projected matrix no longer matches its specification, so the ledger would stop describing what is actually sampled.
assumptions.name: cohort.correlation_psd_gate
assumptions.source: Engineering invariant, not an empirical claim.

assumptions.description: Population health-literacy distribution, not condition-specific.
assumptions.name: cohort.health_literacy_mix
assumptions.source: Approximate adult population shape from health-literacy surveys.

assumptions.description: Share of personas recorded outside the female/male binary.
assumptions.name: cohort.other_sex_fraction
assumptions.source: Modelling convention so downstream code exercises the third option.

assumptions.description:
Pairwise correlations between persona trait axes, fed to the Gaussian copula. Keys are 'axis_a|axis_b'. Convention: higher = 'more' of what the axis is named, so caregiver_support 0.9 means well supported.

SEMANTICS (decided once, do not mix): these are LATENT GAUSSIAN correlations — the rho of the copula's underlying normal, which is what a copula fit to real data would estimate. They are NOT the correlations you will measure on the generated cohort. Pushing rho through the copula attenuates it to (6/pi)*arcsin(rho/2) on the uniforms (0.45 -> 0.4334), and discretising into a categorical or count marginal attenuates it substantially further. That is expected and quantified, not error.

A pair omitted here is asserted UNCORRELATED. Correlation does not propagate through shared neighbours in a correlation matrix, so every relationship that should exist must be listed explicitly.
assumptions.name: cohort.trait_correlations
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. Directions are well supported by health-inequality literature; magnitudes are not fitted to any dataset.

assumptions.description: The model that produces persona speech, and the prompt version it was recorded against. Registered here because swapping a model changes outputs exactly as changing a coefficient does — it is not a config detail. A swap invalidates every cassette (CassetteAdapter refuses to replay across models) and requires re-running the narration evals.
assumptions.name: narration.model
assumptions.source: Chosen for local, offline-first operation. NOT yet exercised against a live model: every compliance number to date comes from scripted stub models written to test the instrument, so this model's actual citation compliance is UNMEASURED. Pass bars are pre-registered in tests/eval/pass_bars.json (before any live run); run scripts/record_narration.py --canary then --record to measure.

assumptions.description: Panel turn order: highest barrier load speaks first. Deterministic and defensible — the most encumbered personas have the most to say about a design, so a truncated session still contains the signal.
assumptions.name: panel.speaking_order
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, NOT a neutral default. Later speakers see the transcript, so the most burdened persona anchors every session. tests/test_narration.py asserts theme sets are stable under a permuted order; if that ever fails, themes are order-fragile and a design review should not lean on them.

assumptions.description: Probability a persona attends a scheduled visit. Logistic in adherence, accumulated burden and barrier load.
assumptions.name: timeline.attendance
assumptions.source: Expert judgement, shaped to give plausible per-visit attendance.

assumptions.description: Per-persona multipliers on burden components, by profile signal. A shift worker weights scheduling friction far above someone retired — the same protocol is not the same ask.
assumptions.name: timeline.burden_sensitivity
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. Magnitudes are illustrative, ordering is the claim.

assumptions.description: Discrete-time dropout hazard evaluated at each visit. Logistic in cumulative burden, barrier load, adherence deficit and consecutive missed visits.
assumptions.name: timeline.dropout_hazard
assumptions.source:
intercept and cumulative_burden_weight are fitted JOINTLY by scripts/calibrate_hazard.py against two anchors — a light protocol (4 remote visits/yr -> 93% retention) and a heavy one (24 visits/yr with diary and washout -> 55%). A mid-intensity 12-visit protocol is HELD OUT and lands at ~81% without being fitted, which is the evidence that the two-parameter form generalises rather than interpolating.

IMPORTANT: the anchors are plausibility targets drawn from commonly reported retention ranges, NOT a fit to any observed dataset. The LEVEL of the curve is an assumption. Only the DIFFERENCE between two designs should be read as signal.

cumulative_burden_weight is FROZEN AT ZERO — unidentifiable from the current anchors, NOT fitted. The two anchors differ mainly in visit count, and count already compounds through survival, so the objective is a flat ridge in this direction: any small value hits both anchors equally well. (An earlier fit returned 0.047; that was the first feasible point on the ridge, i.e. noise, not a calibrated quantity. A number in the ledger reads as calibrated no matter what this note says, so shipping it would have been misleading.) Freezing to zero lets burden_increment_weight carry per-visit burden honestly.

Confirmed dead weight today: with the term at zero, every retention band still holds (light 94.8%, heavy 58.2%, held-out 81.2%) and the fixed-visit-count comparison still separates 12 remote (84.2%) from 12 on-site (81.2%).

THIRD-ANCHOR PLAN: to identify it for real, add an anchor that varies per-visit burden at FIXED visit count (12 on-site vs 12 remote). Then unfreeze and fit intercept + cumulative_burden_weight against the three anchors. Until that anchor exists, do not treat this coefficient as evidence that accumulated burden does or does not matter.

assumptions.description: Burden vector components accrued by one on-site visit, before persona-specific sensitivity is applied. Unitless, roughly 'fraction of one visit's worth of tolerance consumed'.
assumptions.name: timeline.visit_burden
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. The relative shape matters more than the scale.

assumptions.description: Severity assigned to each derived barrier. Feeds the dropout hazard and orders the barrier list a persona narrates from.
assumptions.name: traits.barrier_severity
assumptions.source: Expert judgement. Relative ordering is the defensible part.

disclaimer: Simulated under stated assumptions. Not a forecast, not medical advice, not regulatory evidence. Retention LEVELS are calibrated to plausibility targets rather than fitted to observed data — read the DIFFERENCE between designs, and check `sensitivity` and `assumptions` before quoting anything.

eligibility_attribution.headline: 'age >= 50' is responsible for 100% of total attrition (20.0 of 20 exclusions)
eligibility_attribution.method: Exact Shapley value of the exclusion veto game: each persona's blame is split 1/|failing rules|. No sampling.
